transcript.content: I believe I am ordinary at dance and have no skill at all; this belief leads to self-doubt and low confidence.
[Counselor] Based on your background and the CBT treatment framework, let us focus on the core issue that troubles you most at present.

current_goals: Persistent negative feelings have affected my enjoyment of dance and my overall confidence; I hope that by challenging negative cognitions, gathering evidence, and reframing my perspective, I can shift from 'I have no skill' to 'I am gradually improving through practice and enjoying the process'.
newly_observed: I believe I am ordinary at dance and have no skill at all; this belief leads to self-doubt and low confidence.
payload.main_problem: I believe I am ordinary at dance and have no skill at all; this belief leads to self-doubt and low confidence.
payload.core_demands: Persistent negative feelings have affected my enjoyment of dance and my overall confidence; I hope that by challenging negative cognitions, gathering evidence, and reframing my perspective, I can shift from 'I have no skill' to 'I am gradually improving through practice and enjoying the process'.
growth_experiences: Started attending dance classes a year ago. During a class showcase, other students could complete advanced movements fairly perfectly, but he did not succeed, and felt out of place and ashamed. Afterwards, he frequently compared himself with others in class, saw others as more confident and skilled, and gradually formed a self-evaluation pattern of 'I am ordinary, have no skill, and am not good enough', which recurs every time he dances or thinks about dancing.

special_situations.event: During the class showcase, other students could complete advanced movements while he did not succeed
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot complete the movements as perfectly as my classmates, it means I have no talent and I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubles practice but focuses excessively on errors, mentally dismissing positive feedback to avoid disappointment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not suited to dancing / I have no skill at all

special_situations.event: Receives positive feedback from the instructor or classmates in class (such as 'you are improving', 'you did that move very well')
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only a performance completely without errors is worthy of recognition; others cannot see my real errors, so praise is not credible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores praise, fixates on shortcomings and flaws
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite; I am actually very bad

special_situations.event: In dance class, sees classmates performing more confidently and skillfully
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not as good as them, it proves I am no good / I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly compares with others, lowering self-evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; I am not good enough

special_situations.event: Notices several of his own errors when practicing or reviewing his performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Making mistakes equals failure; errors better represent my true level
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly criticizes himself in his mind, reducing enjoyment of the process
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: As expected, I am no good
